definitions.explanation: Being too friendly or casual with someone you don't know well enough; lacking appropriate social distance.

examples.japanese: ⟦{初対面|しょたいめん}→初対面：07306_shotaimen⟧⟦なのに→のに：10529_noni⟧{馴|な}れ{馴|な}れしい⟦{態度|たいど}→態度：03396_taido⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{取|と}る→取る：00565_toru⟧⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{苦手|にがて}→苦手：03513_nigate⟧⟦だ→だ：09496_da⟧。
examples.english: I don't like people who act overly familiar even though we've just met.

examples.japanese: {馴|な}れ{馴|な}れしく⟦{話|はな}しかけないで→話しかける：03134_hanashikakeru⟧⟦ください→ください：02899_kudasai⟧。
examples.english: Please don't talk to me in such a familiar way.

examples.japanese: ⟦{彼|かれ}→彼：01292_kare⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{馴|な}れ{馴|な}れしさ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{困|こま}っている→困る：00861_komaru⟧。
examples.english: I'm troubled by how overly familiar he is.

examples.japanese: ⟦{客|きゃく}→客：00865_kyaku⟧⟦に{対|たい}して→に対して：06800_nitaishite⟧{馴|な}れ{馴|な}れしい⟦{口調|くちょう}→口調：11803_kuchou⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{失礼|しつれい}→失礼：01247_shitsurei⟧⟦だ→だ：09496_da⟧。
examples.english: Using an overly casual tone with customers is rude.

notes:
{馴|な}れ{馴|な}れしい is an i-adjective formed by doubling ⟦{馴|な}れる→慣れる：00870_nareru⟧ (to become familiar) with the suffix ～しい.

FORMS:
- Adverbial: {馴|な}れ{馴|な}れしく
- Noun form: {馴|な}れ{馴|な}れしさ

USAGE NOTE:
Always carries a negative connotation. It criticizes someone for not maintaining appropriate social boundaries. In Japanese culture, which values proper social distance based on relationship levels, this trait is considered impolite.

COLLOCATIONS:
- {馴|な}れ{馴|な}れしい⟦{態度|たいど}→態度：03396_taido⟧ - overly familiar attitude
- {馴|な}れ{馴|な}れしい⟦{口調|くちょう}→口調：11803_kuchou⟧ - overly casual tone
- {馴|な}れ{馴|な}れしく⟦{接|せっ}する→接する：12920_sessuru⟧ - to treat someone too familiarly

ORTHOGRAPHY:
Often written in hiragana as なれなれしい. The kanji {馴|な}れ is the same as in ⟦{馴染|なじ}む→馴染む：14631_najimu⟧ (to become accustomed).
